title: Finite-field models for lisse coefficient modules
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $X$ with its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the finite coefficient fields $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Write $E_X$ for the pulled-back condensed field ring [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring] and $\Omega_X$ for the pulled-back finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Modules are the internal module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], lisse means pro-etale locally finite free with possibly varying or zero ranks [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], and scalar extensions are the ordinary relative tensor functors [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For every lisse $\Omega_X$-module $L$, there exist a finite coefficient field $E$ and a lisse $E_X$-module $L_E$ together with an isomorphism $\Omega_X\otimes_{E_X}L_E\cong L$. The coefficient inclusion is the canonical map of [def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map]. No nonemptiness or constant-rank hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proof (1), finite affine cover, overlap descent and gluing

proof.text: Remove the invertible condensed coefficient pullback using extendScalarsIsoComapInv and the free transport lemmas. Pull the module along the identity and refine its free cover to a finite affine cover using QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom, preserving freeness by the existing composition and pullback comparisons.

Choose the base coefficient field and on each affine member take the free module of its given rank. The scalar-extension comparison for regular modules and biproducts identifies its extension with the given local trivialization. These modules have finite presentations. Apply the existing finite local-model gluing theorem to obtain a common finite enlargement and a global model, retaining its local identifications. This theorem implements the same finite overlap descent and sheaf-gluing step as the blueprint.

Transport the glued model along the identity coefficient comparison. Its local identifications, pullback/scalar comparison, and preservation of finite free modules prove that it is lisse. The naturality square of the coefficient comparison, scalar-extension transitivity, and the module identity-pullback isomorphism identify its algebraic-closure extension with the original module. All maps are the existing canonical comparisons.

proof_origin.note: Finite affine free local models and the existing common finite enlargement/gluing theorem; canonical coefficient transport returns the actual lisse model.

theorem exists_lisse_finiteCoefficient_model [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (L : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (padicAlgClRingObj X ℓ))
    (hL : IsLisseCoefficientModule (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) L) :
    ∃ (E : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields ℓ (PadicAlgCl ℓ))
      (L_E : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
        (padicSubfieldRingObj X ℓ E)),
      IsLisseCoefficientModule (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) L_E ∧
        Nonempty ((Mod.extendScalars (padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl X ℓ E)).obj L_E ≅ L)
